I farm 12.4 mu, and I have to keep the plan practical because my household labor is limited and some family members work off-farm. I also have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect yield instead of gambling on rainfall. Since my main system is wheat-maize, I will keep most of the land in that rotation because it is familiar, fits my experience, and spreads income across the year. I will keep a smaller part in stevia because it gives me diversification, but I will not let it take too much land since it needs careful management. For wheat, I will use improved seed, steady fertilizer, and a few irrigations to secure a stable grain yield. After wheat harvest, I will put that same land straight into hybrid maize because I want strong summer yield and better performance. For stevia, I will manage it more carefully on a smaller area with moderate fertilizer, enough water, and more pest watching because quality matters. I will keep tillage simple with rotary tillage where it saves labor, and I will avoid making the plan too heavy in inputs because I want returns without unnecessary cost.
